races.name: Happy 70th Birthday Brian Glanville Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Safari Dream
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with solid good-ground form over 6f including a recent win in identical conditions (1/6f/GOO), handled ably by Oisin Murphy; a natural hold-up type who has won from off the pace here and is the chief danger if able to slot into second or third behind the leader rather than being buried at the tail of this hold-up-heavy field.
runners_data.comment: Third last time out and a winner four starts back, Safari Dream arrives here fit on a 20-day turnaround with experience of today's trip and going, and his rating of 82 puts him top of this field — draw one the only neutral unknown.

runners_data.name: Newsreader
runners_data.note: Tony Carroll's five-year-old has been modest in recent outings (three consecutive sixth-place finishes) and its true deep hold-up style means it is likely to be pushed even further back than the map suggests in a field saturated with closers; Rossa Ryan will need a lot to go right from 33 days off the track.
runners_data.comment: Newsreader has run over today's trip and going, and our rating of 79 marks him out as a serious threat from stall 5 — the third he recorded five starts back gives hope, but he's been winless in recent starts and will need to find more to break through.

runners_data.name: Escape Plan
runners_data.note: Tom Ward's lightly-raced three-year-old showed ability when second on soft, but the 74-day absence (no headgear, no trainer 14-day strike rate) is a concern, and its hold-up style leaves it reliant on a well-paced race it is unlikely to get given Diamondinthedark's control; best watched for now.
runners_data.comment: Escape Plan won three starts back but has finished eighth twice since, and 74 days off the track adds a fitness query; he has run over today's trip and carries 136 lb from stall four.

runners_data.name: Diamondinthedark
runners_data.note: Mark Loughnane's three-year-old has the race by the throat tactically — its 1/6f/STA and 2/6f/STA form confirms a natural front-runner who has won and placed when allowed to dominate; Billy Loughnane should find a clean lead in a small field and the style-fit flag merely reflects the mapped position rather than any real role mismatch.
runners_data.comment: A winner two starts back but beaten into eighth last time out, Diamondinthedark heads into this on a 61-day absence and rates below most rivals on our figures; she has run over today's trip, at least, but this looks tough from stall seven off 135 lb.

runners_data.name: Monsieur Patat
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old David Egan partner with two wins and four places on good ground (8/15 runs), though recent form has been patchy and it is a genuine hold-up type that will be pushed to the very rear of this already congested closing group; trip and going suit in theory but the redistribution from the rear of the pack is a real structural problem.

runners_data.name: The Coffee Pod
runners_data.note: William Muir and Chris Grassick's five-year-old is back quickly (10 days) and carries headgear, but its form figures over 6f on good ground are uniformly poor (5th, 7th, 8th); another deep closer that cannot get its natural position in this field and faces a steep ask off a low OR of 62.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, The Coffee Pod nevertheless carries a rating of 76 against an official mark of 62, suggesting he is better than his recent finishes imply — he has run over today's distance and going, and 10 days since his last run leaves him fresh. The risk is that those fifths, sevenths and eighths are hard to look past.

runners_data.name: The Feminine Urge
runners_data.note: Grace Harris's four-year-old has placed form on good ground over 6f (2nd and 3rd in last two) and Seamus Cronin claims 5lb, making the weight attractive at OR 57; a natural hold-up type that will race wide and deep with the rest of the closers, and the apprentice will need a generous pace and clear daylight late to land a blow.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last six starts and ranked last on our figures, The Feminine Urge faces a stiff task from stall 2 carrying 127 lb — though she arrives fit on a 10-day turnaround, has run over today's distance and going before, and back-to-back placed efforts last time out and two starts back offer a sliver of hope.

races.paceDynamic: Diamondinthedark is the one confirmed front-runner here and, with just seven runners on a flat 6f at Ffos Las, Billy Loughnane is likely to find a clean lead and control every fraction of this race from the off. The pace should be sustainable rather than suicidal — a lone pace-setter dictating on good ground shapes up as a genuine advantage, giving the leader a chance to conserve energy through the early exchanges before lengthening in the final two furlongs. The field is heavily loaded with hold-up horses — Safari Dream, Newsreader, Monsieur Patat, The Coffee Pod and The Feminine Urge all want to come from off the pace — but so many closers chasing a single, unhurried leader on a flat track is a structurally awkward scenario for that group. This race shape most clearly favours horses who can either track Diamondinthedark closely in second or third, or a well-judged hold-up horse with exceptional finishing speed; the mid-to-rear pack will be doing near-identical work and the decisive factor will be which one gets the clearest run late. The field holds more genuine hold-up types than the positional map can accommodate at the rear — Newsreader, Monsieur Patat, The Coffee Pod and The Feminine Urge are all true deep closers redistributed forward on the map, but in reality Diamondinthedark and Safari Dream are most likely to physically secure the prominent positions.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Lone Leader Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Diamondinthedark gets an uncontested lead and sets a measured, confidence-building tempo that the hold-up pack cannot bridge.
scenarios.body: Diamondinthedark dictates every fraction with Loughnane in full control, the pace never rising to a level that invites closers to close the gap, and the leader's stamina reserves allow a kick through the final furlong; the 21-8 form line and strong stall-to-lead profile make this the most structurally coherent outcome.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closest Chaser Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If a horse tracks Diamondinthedark in second or third throughout and pounces in the final furlong as the leader ties up.
scenarios.body: Safari Dream has winning form over 6f at similar pace shapes and with Oisin Murphy aboard can be positioned to track and deliver a powerful late challenge without covering excess ground; the hold-up crowd racing uniformly from the rear give Safari Dream a gap in the slipstream profile that a well-timed move exploits.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If Diamondinthedark sets an unexpectedly strong early pace that weakens its own finishing speed and opens a late window for the deepest closers.
scenarios.body: The Feminine Urge has placed form on good ground over 6f and Monsieur Patat has shown the ability to produce a sustained late run when the pace is honest, both needing a genuine end-to-end gallop to get competitive; this scenario depends on Diamondinthedark overcooking it, which looks unlikely given the low runner count and likely comfort in front.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Squeeze Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the redistributed hold-up horses find themselves bottled up behind a slow pace and one breaks free with a well-timed switch to get a clear run.
scenarios.body: Newsreader or The Coffee Pod would need a combination of a slow early tempo — creating bunching — and a fortunate split in traffic to manufacture the space their true style needs to flourish; both carry meaningful style-fit discounts given they are racing out of their natural role and their recent form on good ground offers limited encouragement.

watchPoints.text: Diamondinthedark — watch whether Billy Loughnane actually secures the lead cleanly from the gates; if anything pushes wide for position and disrupts the front-running plan, the entire race shape changes.

Safari Dream — Oisin Murphy's ability to position this hold-up type closer than usual (second or third) rather than at the tail will be crucial; if Murphy is forced wide or deep into a crowded closing pack, the structural edge for this horse dissolves.

The Feminine Urge — Seamus Cronin's 5lb claim is significant at OR 57 and this filly's recent placed form on good ground over 6f warrants monitoring as a potential value closer, but watch whether the apprentice can navigate traffic cleanly given how many hold-up horses will be racing in the same finishing ground.

Monsieur Patat — David Egan's involvement elevates this aged sprinter slightly, but watch market moves; if support comes despite the structural redistribution problem, it may signal an improved piece of work or stable confidence not visible in the form string.

races.name: Ebf Novice Stakes (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Perfect Nation
runners_data.note: Won over 7f at Sandown last time and placed at Goodwood on good, giving her the strongest profile in the field; Billy Loughnane is an assertive front-riding partner and George Boughey's yard is in solid form (6/28 over 14 days), making her the clear pace anchor here.

runners_data.name: Artemis Star
runners_data.note: Finished fifth on debut over 6f on good going for William Muir & Chris Grassick, so the step up to 7½f is a logical progression for a lightly-raced type; running style is uncertain, and her hind-shoes headgear change is worth noting as a possible signal that connections want more focus.

runners_data.name: Avionics
runners_data.note: Placed in a 7f maiden on good going last time which shows the trip and conditions suit, but he is a genuine hold-up horse whom the pace map has pushed into a midfield slot purely because the rear is crowded; Andrew Balding's yard is operating at a strong 11/54 strike rate over 14 days.

runners_data.name: First Mate
runners_data.note: Trailed in seventh on debut over 6f on good ground, so there is little to recommend from the form book; a natural hold-up horse whose best hope rests on the pace collapsing, but being mapped out of his preferred rear position weakens that already slim prospect.

runners_data.name: George Cross
runners_data.note: An unraced debutant from Owen Burrows, who has had no runners in the past 14 days, and running style is completely unknown; the absence of any form string means this horse could land anywhere on the track and any positive result would be driven by raw talent alone.

runners_data.name: Midgham Man
runners_data.note: Finished fifth on debut at Windsor over 6f on good and has Oisin Murphy booked, which is a clear upgrade in ride; 36 days between runs is the longest freshener in this field, and as a hold-up horse in an uncontested-pace race he will need a strong gallop to close.

runners_data.name: Revoked
runners_data.note: Finished a distant ninth over 7f on good last time and is tagged as a horse who fades in the finish — the worst possible profile in a race where the front-runner is expected to dominate at a controlled pace; Clive Cox sends him back quickly (18 days) but the profile asks a lot.

races.paceDynamic: Perfect Nation is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with no genuine pace rival to challenge her, she is likely to coast into an uncontested lead and control the tempo from the front on good ground over 7½f at Ffos Las. The hold-up contingent — Avionics, First Mate, Midgham Man, and Revoked — will be strung out behind her, with Artemis Star and George Cross (both unknown/unproven in style) filling the middle ground. This field contains more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear; First Mate and Avionics are genuine hold-up horses who have been redistributed to midfield positions because the rear is overcrowded, meaning their true closing power may be partially compromised. The race shape overwhelmingly favours Perfect Nation dictating a controlled, honest gallop that saps the finishing kick from the closers — front-running and prominent profiles are best placed here.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Perfect Nation Leads Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Perfect Nation breaks cleanly and is allowed to stride into an uncontested lead, controlling tempo throughout.
scenarios.body: She sets a sustainable pace on good ground, conserves energy through the bend and lengthens in the straight before her rivals can mount a meaningful challenge; her Goodwood win on similar going and Billy Loughnane's positive front-running style suit this perfectly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Mow Her Down Late
scenarios.trigger: If Perfect Nation goes too fast early or ties up in the final furlong, allowing the hold-up horses to swarm past.
scenarios.body: A solo leader who has gone a fraction too quick finds herself a sitting target as the straight arrives; Midgham Man or Revoked, if they get a clear run from the back, would be the beneficiaries of a collapsing front-runner.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Debut Wildcard Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If George Cross, the unraced runner from Owen Burrows' yard, is significantly better than his rivals on debut and produces a performance that overrides the pace map.
scenarios.body: An unknown quantity with no form string can upset any shape analysis if the latent ability is there; Burrows is capable of producing well-prepared debutants and Callum Rodriguez gives him a competent partner.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Midfield Prominent Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed hold-up types manages to slot into a genuine prominent position and tracks Perfect Nation closely enough to challenge turning in.
scenarios.body: First Mate or Avionics, if they secure a better position than their natural style suggests, could benefit from sitting second or third and picking off a tired leader; this scenario is discounted because both are true hold-up horses racing out of role.

watchPoints.text: Watch Perfect Nation's break from the stalls — if she jumps cleanly under Billy Loughnane she will be unopposed and the race is effectively over as a pace contest.

Monitor whether First Mate or Avionics push forward at the start rather than settling in their redistributed midfield slots — either breaking their natural hold-up pattern would briefly change the complexion of the race.
George Cross is a complete unknown on debut for Owen Burrows and could trade at a misleading price; any hint of market support late should be noted as connections' confidence signal.

Revoked's "fades in finish" tag combined with a ninth-place debut run makes him the most vulnerable horse if the gallop is even half-controlled — watch whether Rossa Ryan opts for an aggressive early position as a tactical change.

Midgham Man has Oisin Murphy aboard, a significant jockey booking for a barn at 7/19; watch how Murphy positions him in the first two furlongs — a closer to the front than expected would suggest connections believe the hold-up tactic is not viable in this field.

races.name: Ken Meredith Memorial Race Handicap Stakes (Div I)

runners_data.name: Lerwick
runners_data.note: Hold-up specialist on Good going with reasonable course-and-distance profile, but sim-going record of 0 wins and 0 places from five attempts in similar conditions is a concern; 12-day turnaround is fresh enough and Billy Loughnane claims experience, but the deep draw and need for a strong pace make this a tough ask.|
runners_data.comment: Lerwick has been running into form of late, finishing third five starts back before a sequence of placed-to-near-placed efforts, and he drops into this race carrying 141 lb from stall 8 with experience over today's trip and going; the concern is he remains winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: Sofian
runners_data.note: Ryan Kavanagh takes off 3lb for a horse that has won and placed on Good ground at around this trip, and the form figures of 1-2 in better-ground races are the most relevant here; however Sofian is a genuine hold-up type who will likely be forced to race closer than ideal given the volume of closers in this field, mildly compromising his finishing kick.|
runners_data.comment: Sofian shaped well when third last time out and has previous experience over today's trip and going, with his rating of 68 suggesting he holds more in hand than his mark implies — the risk is that two disappointing efforts before that recent revival leave his consistency open to question.

runners_data.name: Bird Of War
runners_data.note: Charles Hills sends this lightly-raced three-year-old 40 days fresh, and while his OR-65 marks him as the highest-rated in the field, he has failed to fire in five consecutive outings and a 0W0P record on similar going over this sort of trip raises genuine questions about whether he fires on Good turf.|
runners_data.comment: Bird Of War arrives here third last time out and a winner four starts back, with experience of today's trip and going working in his favour. Forty days between runs is the query, but our rating of 74 just edges him to the top of this nine-runner field.

runners_data.name: Cypriot Diaspora
runners_data.note: The only confirmed front-runner, handing Oisin Murphy a golden tactical opportunity to control this race from start to finish; his sim-going record of 1W2P from 15 attempts suggests he can be effective on Good, and while his recent form is modest, his role as sole pace-setter at Ffos Las is a significant structural advantage here.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Cypriot Diaspora at least showed a return to form with a third last time out, and she has experience over today's distance and going; carrying 136 lb from stall four, she looks a midfield proposition at best.

runners_data.name: Our Dagger
runners_data.note: Returning from a long 127-day absence for Adrian Wintle who has placed 4 from 14 runners in the past fortnight — fitness must be respected as a question mark; Our Dagger is a natural hold-up horse who in this crowded-closers field will be pushed back further than he'd want, and his sim-going record of 0W0P from three Good-ground starts gives little encouragement.|
runners_data.comment: A lengthy absence of 127 days and no placed effort in his last four starts make Our Dagger hard to fancy, and he is ranked seventh of nine on our figures; he does carry experience of today's distance and going, and stall two is his draw.

runners_data.name: Thestral
runners_data.note: Wears a hood (hg:p) and showed genuine form with a second and a third at this sort of trip earlier in the year; the 27-day fresher spell suits a horse who has run five times this season, and Rossa Ryan is a sharp judge of pace, but this three-year-old has yet to win and needs others to play into his hands in the straight.|
runners_data.comment: Thestral shaped with promise when third and second in consecutive starts, and having run over today's distance and going before, he retains strong claims at 134 lb from stall 5 — though he remains winless in recent starts, and that elusive breakthrough is the key question.

runners_data.name: Laughterintherain
runners_data.note: The only genuine prominent-style racer aside from the front-runner, giving Kieran Shoemark a clear map — sit second, save ground, challenge two furlongs out; Ed Walker's operation is in strong form (T14: 8/34) and this horse's 42-day break could mean he returns sharper, though 0W0P on Good ground over this trip is a note of caution.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Laughterintherain has experience of today's distance and going, but her recent string of mid-to-rear finishes is hard to ignore; a second four starts back offers a crumb of hope, though 42 days off and a tough task from stall one make this a guarded read.

runners_data.name: Ebn Sabt
runners_data.note: Wears a hood and visor (hg:pv), signalling a horse that needs anchoring mentally; a true hold-up type who has not won in 13 starts on comparable going and whose recent form figures (467707) contain nothing to inspire confidence — the style-fit penalty applies as he will be pressed into a midfield role that does not suit his natural finishing pattern.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last six starts, with three sevenths among his recent finishes, Ebn Sabt is hard to fancy ranked bottom of nine on our figures, though he has run over today's trip before and 34 days between runs suggests he arrives fresh.

runners_data.name: Grand Vista
runners_data.note: A lightly-raced three-year-old for Muir and Grassick, returning 14 days after a run; has placed on Good going and over 7f, and the apprentice Lewis Edmunds has experience on this horse — but as a natural hold-up type forced into midfield by a crowded rear-guard, the realistic ceiling in this race shape is a minor placing unless chaos unfolds ahead.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts and ranked eighth of nine on our figures, Grand Vista faces a stiff task here; third two starts back offers a crumb of encouragement, and he has run over today's trip before, but the overall profile makes him hard to fancy.

races.paceDynamic: Cypriot Diaspora is the sole confirmed front-runner in this nine-runner handicap over 7½f at Ffos Las and, with no rival likely to seriously press for the lead, Oisin Murphy can dictate a measured, sustainable gallop from the front. Laughterintherain is the only genuine prominent-style runner and will likely track Cypriot Diaspora into second position, leaving the rest to operate from midfield or further back. The field is heavily stacked with hold-up types — Sofian, Our Dagger, Ebn Sabt and Grand Vista are all true closers but have been redistributed to midfield on the map because there simply is not enough rear-guard room to place them all naturally; of these, Sofian and Ebn Sabt are likeliest to actually secure the closest position to the leaders. With a single uncontested pace-setter controlling proceedings on Good ground, this race shape strongly favours either Cypriot Diaspora itself if the pace proves untroubling, or a single closest-pursuer who can travel smoothly just behind and quicken at the two-furlong pole — the prominent-to-midfield profile sitting two to three lengths off the leader is the sweet spot.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cypriot Diaspora Controls Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If Cypriot Diaspora secures the lead without a serious early challenge and Murphy sets an honest but unforced pace.
scenarios.body: Cypriot Diaspora dictates every inch of the race on his own terms, ensuring no excessive early burn, and reaches the straight with enough in reserve to repel challengers on Good ground over a trip he has placed at before. Murphy's class advantage in a low-grade handicap from the front is significant, and runners forced wide or deep from hold-up positions will struggle to close a controlled gap.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Runs On
scenarios.trigger: If Laughterintherain tracks Cypriot Diaspora comfortably and outstays him in the final furlong as the pace bleeds from the leader.
scenarios.body: Shoemark on Laughterintherain sits a length or two behind the leader, travels within himself on the Good turf, and produces a clean challenge entering the final furlong that Cypriot Diaspora cannot match if the front-runner has given too much. Laughterintherain's third-year profile over 7f suits this position, and the proximity to the pace means no ground needs to be made up from deep.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Arrive Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough to soften the front two and the hold-up horses find a clear passage in the straight.
scenarios.body: A sustainable but honest gallop could still leave the field bunched turning in, allowing a horse who has switched off behind the pace and found a gap to finish powerfully through the closing stages. Sofian has the best going form of the hold-up types on Good and Thestral showed placed form at this trip, making them the most credible beneficiaries if the race truly comes to them.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Handicap Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If the race fragments badly, several horses fail to get their positions and the pace becomes uneven or collapses in the straight.
scenarios.body: Without competitive pressure from genuine rivals, Cypriot Diaspora's fractions may be deceptive — either crawling early and sprinting, or going too fast and stopping — creating a lottery in the final two furlongs. In this scenario a horse with tactical versatility or an unexposed profile such as Grand Vista or Bird Of War, tracking from midfield, could snatch a place or more from a scrambled finish.

watchPoints.text: Cypriot Diaspora's early-race fractions are the key to everything — if Murphy elects to creep along rather than set a true pace, the entire field will be compressed turning in and the handicap becomes a sprint lottery rather than a staying test.

Laughterintherain must secure the position directly behind Cypriot Diaspora before the first bend; if Sofian or Ebn Sabt push forward and take that rail spot, Shoemark could find himself trapped three or four wide for most of the race.

Our Dagger's 127-day absence is the longest in the field by some margin — watch his market moves in the morning as a guide to whether Wintle is genuinely confident, and note whether he shows any sign of greenness or ring-rustiness at the start.

With four redistributed hold-up horses all needing to find gaps in the straight simultaneously, watch for significant traffic incidents in the final two furlongs — especially if the field fans wide approaching the line and jostling occurs between Sofian, Ebn Sabt, Grand Vista and Our Dagger.|

races.name: Ken Meredith Memorial Race Handicap Stakes (Div II)

runners_data.name: Manhattan Mirage
runners_data.note: A natural hold-up performer with sim-going form of just 4 runs and no wins or placings on good, carrying 60 days of ring rust; pushed into the midfield on the map because the field is saturated with closers, meaning it will race even further back than shown and faces a near-impossible task in this shape.|
runners_data.comment: Manhattan Mirage has experience of today's trip and conditions, and a rating of 73 suggests he is better than his official mark of 62 implies — the main risk is that he has been winless in recent starts and returns after 60 days off.

runners_data.name: Rosemary's Rose
runners_data.note: Oisin Murphy takes the ride for Rod Millman, who is in strong form (7/19 over 14 days), and this mare has placed twice in her last four starts including a second on soft and a second on standard — the step to good ground is not a concern and she holds a clean prominent position in a race that sets up perfectly for her tracking style.|
runners_data.comment: Rosemary's Rose has been knocking consistently on the door, finishing second twice and third last time out in her last three starts, and she has run over today's trip and going — the risk is that she remains yet to win despite that fine recent consistency.

runners_data.name: Venturing
runners_data.note: William Carson partners this 3-year-old hold-up type who has placed once on good in four similar-going starts; the drop from 8f back to 7½f is worth noting, and while the form string of 4-4-9-7 gives little confidence, the good ground and a race likely run at a steady tempo at least keeps the possibility of a late run alive.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last four starts, with a pair of fourth-place finishes his best recent efforts, Venturing looks hard to fancy ranked eighth of nine on our figures; he has run over today's trip and returns after 33 days, but there is little in the profile to inspire confidence.

runners_data.name: Speculative
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's runner has been off 73 days and the yard is without a win in eight runners over the past fortnight — the layoff and trainer form are both red flags; three of four runs on good ground have returned 7th, 4th and 9th, and as a hold-up type in a race that will not suit closers, improvement looks hard to find here.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last four starts, Speculative nevertheless catches the eye with experience over today's trip and conditions, and our rating of 76 makes her a leading threat from stall one; the concern is that recent form has been disappointing, with back-to-back finishes outside the first eight.

runners_data.name: March Of Time
runners_data.note: The confirmed sole front-runner in the race, Rossa Ryan can set his own terms on good going that he has encountered in all three career starts (5th, 4th, 3rd), and the fact that he steps up from 6f to 7½f for the first time is the key unknown — he has always been pace-prominent and the flat Ffos Las track gives him every chance of controlling proceedings.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts, March Of Time does show a degree of consistency — third three starts back — but her more recent fifth and fourth suggest she's struggling to progress; carrying 135 lb from stall nine makes the task no easier.

runners_data.name: Piazza
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides a 3-year-old who has placed in four of seven starts, including two thirds on good ground, and the 7f trip is well within range — a natural hold-up type who has shown the ability to finish off races on good, and the Ollie Sangster yard has been placing horses to win (7/16 T14), making this one of the more interesting holding-up profiles in the race.|
runners_data.comment: Piazza has been knocking on the door, with a pair of thirds three and four starts back, though she has drifted to seventh last time out and remains winless in recent starts; our rating of 78 makes her the one to beat here, and she returns after 19 days carrying 134 lb from stall 5.

runners_data.name: Kaleidoscope Eyes
runners_data.note: Bernard Llewellyn's charge won over 8f at Hereford on heavy and has three of five good-ground runs return single-figure finishing positions, suggesting the surface is fine; however, it is a genuine hold-up horse that has been mapped to the midfield purely due to overcrowding at the rear, meaning it will likely be stationed even further back and faces a significant positional disadvantage in a race not run to suit.|
runners_data.comment: Third last time out gives Kaleidoscope Eyes a recent placed effort to build on, and she has experience over today's trip and going; however, the unplaced run in behind that finish and 132 lb to carry are real tests of her resolve.

runners_data.name: Cosmic Jive
runners_data.note: Flagged for fading in the finish, this Kieran Shoemark-ridden 3-year-old has form figures of 8-7-8 in three starts, all on softer ground than today's good — the surface switch may not help, and as a true hold-up type repositioned into the midfield on the map, it is racing against its grain in a race shape that will not generate the pace it needs to close.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with three consecutive finishes of eighth, seventh, and eighth, Cosmic Jive is hard to fancy at the bottom of our rankings; he has run over today's trip before, and 37 days off at least suggests he returns fresh from stall two carrying 130 lb.

runners_data.name: Iconic Dawn
runners_data.note: Hughie Morrison's youngster has headgear noted (blinkers) and has been off 14 days, but the form of 3-5-0-7-11 on today's ground of good (2 from 6 similar going) gives little to work with; a genuine rear-of-field type displaced into the midfield on the map, it is among the most compromised horses in the race by the congested hold-up group and the steady pace set by the lone leader.|
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts and only seventh last time out, Iconic Dawn is hard to fancy from draw 3, though she has run over today's distance and going before and her fitness is fine at 14 days since last race.

races.paceDynamic: March Of Time is the sole confirmed front-runner here and, with no obvious challenger for the lead, Rossa Ryan should be able to bowl along at a controlled, honest gallop on good ground over 7½f at Ffos Las — a pace that suits a horse travelling within itself rather than setting a searing tempo. Behind him, the field is stacked with genuine hold-up types: Manhattan Mirage, Cosmic Jive, Kaleidoscope Eyes and Iconic Dawn are all natural closers who have been pushed forward on the pace map simply because there is nowhere else to put them, meaning the midfield will be congested and those horses will not get the wide-open run their style demands. Rosemary's Rose and Piazza, as the most credible prominent horses, are best placed to track March Of Time in the slipstream and pounce entering the straight. This race shape — a lone, unhurried front-runner setting a sustainable pace — overwhelmingly favours horses racing prominently or in a close-tracking position, as the hold-up contingent will likely find themselves bottled up in a traffic-heavy midfield with insufficient run to the line to make up meaningful ground. The field holds materially more hold-up horses than the map can accommodate at the rear; among those most likely to actually secure a prominent position behind March Of Time are Rosemary's Rose and Piazza, with the redistributed closers likely to be further back than ideal.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Lead, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If March Of Time dictates a sustainable gallop unchallenged and the prominent trackers have enough left to quicken at the two-furlong pole.
scenarios.body: March Of Time sets a measured pace and the horses travelling closest in his wake — Rosemary's Rose and Piazza — get the ideal tow into the straight before unleashing their finish on good ground. Hold-up horses struggle to pick their way through a congested midfield in time to land a serious blow.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: March Of Time Fronts Up
scenarios.trigger: If March Of Time is allowed to stride clear unchallenged and builds enough of a cushion that he is never truly reeled in.
scenarios.body: Rossa Ryan, a big-race jockey on a horse with a clear front-running profile stepped into a tactically simple spot, finds every fence on the rail and simply outstays a field of closers who cannot close the gap in time. The good ground suits a horse that has form figures of 3-4-5 exclusively on going better than good-soft, and a clear lead on a flat, fair track amplifies his natural advantage.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late-Closing Traffic Nightmare
scenarios.trigger: If the midfield becomes a bottleneck and one horse threads through late to steal a place, rather than win outright.
scenarios.body: With so many true hold-up types compressed into the middle of the pack, a single well-timed split could allow one closer to emerge, but the pace is unlikely to be strong enough to set it up for a decisive late burst from the rear. Piazza, with solid placed form on good ground and Tom Marquand in the saddle, is the most likely beneficiary of any late opening, though winning from this position in this shape remains difficult.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Closers Swamp
scenarios.trigger: If March Of Time goes too fast too soon — against his usual profile — and blows up, leaving the field to sprint for home.
scenarios.body: This scenario is the least likely given March Of Time's measured racing style and the lack of any pace pressure to force his hand, but if he does overextend, the closers theoretically have a chance. In practice, the redistributed hold-up types (Manhattan Mirage, Cosmic Jive, Iconic Dawn) are racing out of role throughout and are unlikely to be positioned to capitalise even if the race falls apart up front.

watchPoints.text: March Of Time (Rossa Ryan) will dictate every aspect of the pace from the front — watch whether he steals an uncontested lead of two lengths or more by the halfway point, because if he does, the hold-up dominated field will have extreme difficulty closing the gap.|

Rosemary's Rose must get away cleanly from her draw and secure a prominent position immediately — if she gets shuffled back into the congested midfield bloc in the early stages, her chance is materially reduced even though her profile suits the pace shape best.|

The midfield is likely to become a traffic jam between the 4f and 2f poles, given that Manhattan Mirage, Cosmic Jive, Kaleidoscope Eyes and Iconic Dawn are all true hold-up horses crammed into the same section of the field — watch for interference or a horse being severely checked when gaps close.|

Piazza (Tom Marquand) is the one hold-up type with a realistic chance of threading late if any gaps appear — Marquand's positional awareness makes him the rider most likely to exploit any opening in the final two furlongs.|

Speculative's 73-day absence combined with Dascombe's 0/8 T14 record makes it one to monitor for sluggish early pace — if it misses the break and trails the field, it is essentially a non-runner in a race that will not be run fast enough to bring it back into contention.|

races.name: Golwg Gwendraeth Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Mythological Star
runners_data.note: Best RPR in the field at 72 and handles Good ground (1 place from 3 sim-going runs); Billy Loughnane rides a hold-up horse who will need to be produced late from what is a compressed, steadily-run race — 29 days off is manageable and the Kubler yard post a T14 of 3/11 suggesting quiet current form.
runners_data.comment: Mythological Star has been placed third in each of his last two starts and, having run over today's trip and going, returns here in good order after 29 days; winless in his recent starts, but his consistency and a rating of 73 make him the one to beat from stall four.

runners_data.name: Station Bar
runners_data.note: Won over this course and distance at Ffos Las last time, which is a significant angle; though its natural style is hold-up, it has been remapped to the front as the sole likely pace-setter, and the 0.80 STYLE_FIT reflects genuine uncertainty over whether it will lead willingly — Eve Johnson Houghton's T14 of 2/33 is a concern.
runners_data.comment: Station Bar won two starts back and has experience of today's trip and conditions, with a 130 lb burden from stall 1 the key watch point — that fifth last time out is the one question mark he needs to answer.

runners_data.name: Gelato
runners_data.note: Sole win came at 8f on Soft for Adrian Wintle, so there is a going and trip match, but the horse is a true rear-of-field type now forced into a midfield position on the map; 48 days off and a T14 of 4/14 suggest the yard is ticking along, yet the 0.91 STYLE_FIT discount tempers expectations in a race that may not play to its strengths.
runners_data.comment: Gelato lands a win last time out and has experience of both today's trip and conditions, making her a serious threat from stall two at 129 lb; the 48-day absence is the one question mark over her sharpness.

runners_data.name: Somethingintheair
runners_data.note: 244 days off the track is a major flag and demands caution regardless of any other factor; David Egan takes the ride on a horse whose last three runs all came on Standard going at 7-8f, and while the trip is not a concern, the lengthy layoff and JS Moore's modest T14 of 3/16 make this one to treat carefully until showing it retains its ability.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last three starts and not seen on a racecourse for 244 days, Somethingintheair faces a stiff ask on return; she has run over today's trip, but with our rating ranking her fifth of five, it's hard to make a strong case.

runners_data.name: Hurricane Laughter
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's yard is in excellent current form with a T14 of 8/34, which is the standout trainer angle in this field; Kieran Shoemark rides a genuine hold-up performer who has three runs on Good ground at this distance and sits just 19 days off its last start — though it maps to midfield rather than its preferred rear position, the yard form gives it a plausible each-way claim.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts, Hurricane Laughter nonetheless brings strong distance and going experience to the table, and 19 days since his last run leaves him fresh; the concern is that his recent finishes — his latest fourth the best in that sequence — suggest he must find more to land a blow here.

races.paceDynamic: Station Bar is the only confirmed front runner in this field and, redistributed to the lead from a true hold-up profile, will set a sustainable, uncontested gallop around Ffos Las's flat mile on Good ground. With no natural pace rival to press him, the tempo is likely to be measured rather than searching, meaning the race is likely to develop as a steadily-run affair before quickening in the final two furlongs. That controlled pace dynamic typically suits horses who can travel prominently or make smooth headway from midfield — it does not create the deep, end-to-end gallop that genuine hold-up finishers need. Gelato, Somethingintheair and Hurricane Laughter are all true hold-up horses remapped to midfield because this field holds far more rear-of-field types than the race shape can accommodate at the back, and none of them is guaranteed to get their natural position; Station Bar is the most likely to at least approximate its shown position, though it is racing out of its true role.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Steady Pace, Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Station Bar sets a controlled, uncontested tempo and the field bunches through the middle mile, triggering a sprint finish from midfield.
scenarios.body: Station Bar's modest front-running from a redistributed position creates a false-paced race where the final two furlongs become a sprint, favouring horses with tactical speed who can travel close to the pace without being exposed early. Mythological Star and Hurricane Laughter, best placed to settle and produce a late run in a race that doesn't truly test stamina, are the primary beneficiaries of this compressed finish.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Station Bar Steals It
scenarios.trigger: If Station Bar, despite racing out of its natural role, is allowed to build a soft lead and the field fails to organise a coherent challenge.
scenarios.body: With no genuine pace-presser to close him down, Station Bar could steal several lengths on the field through the final turn and simply not be caught if the pace behind him is slow to wind up. This shape suits a lone leader who dictates on their own terms, and a STYLE_FIT discount of 0.80 means this is possible but not the likeliest outcome.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horses Emerge
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses dramatically in the home straight and a genuine late run from the back of the field becomes viable.
scenarios.body: Gelato or Somethingintheair, despite being pushed out of their preferred rear position by redistribution, could benefit if they manage to drop away and produce a sustained finish from off the pace. The risk is significant because neither is guaranteed a clear passage in a compressed five-runner field, and both carry STYLE_FIT discounts that temper confidence in this unfolding cleanly.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Contested Early, Attrition
scenarios.trigger: If the pace unexpectedly lifts in the first half-mile due to position-jostling among the hold-up types reluctant to settle at the back.
scenarios.body: A more pressured early gallop would stretch the field and reward the horse with the most genuine stamina for a flat mile on Good ground, making this a true test rather than a sprint finish. Mythological Star, who has shown consistency at this trip and similar going, and Hurricane Laughter, with three runs at a mile in Good conditions, are best equipped if endurance rather than acceleration decides the outcome.

watchPoints.text: Hurricane Laughter — Walker's T14 of 8/34 is the best trainer angle in the race; watch for Shoemark positioning it with cover in midfield from the outset, which may signal a serious each-way market move.

Station Bar — if it refuses to settle at the front after redistribution out of its natural hold-up role, it could burn through petrol early and capitulate in the final furlong, dramatically changing the shape of the finish.

Somethingintheair — 244 days off is the longest absence in the field and should flag as a potential non-trier or fitness concern; watch the market for any significant drifting in the minutes before post time.

Mythological Star — with the highest OR (72) and Loughnane in the saddle, watch whether it is settled toward the rear or asked to race more prominently; its tactical deployment will signal whether the Kубlers are expecting a forward showing.

Gelato — the sole previous win came on Soft, not Good, so watch the going report for any late softening, and monitor whether Finley Marsh drops it out to its natural rear position or attempts to travel closer to the pace given the compressed field.

races.name: Dandara Homes Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Condotti
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse for Hugo Palmer with Oisin Murphy — a top booking — who has shown ability at 10f on good ground (2nd at Goodwood), steps up to 1m4f here which could suit, visor worn; 29 days since last run is fine.
runners_data.comment: Condotti has been knocking on the door in recent starts, finishing second last time out and third two starts back, and he handles today's going — winless in his last five, but our rating just puts him top of this field.

runners_data.name: Beaune
runners_data.note: Dropped in class after a recent 3rd over this 1m4f trip at Sandown, Harry Vigors (5lb claim) keeps costs down; natural closer who has a decent recent profile at longer trips, five outings at 12f+ bodes well for this distance.
runners_data.comment: Beaune ran a solid third last time out and boasts two wins in his last six starts, including a victory five starts back, and he has experience over today's trip and going. The risk is that his form has dipped in recent outings.

runners_data.name: Jimmy Mark
runners_data.note: Rossa Ryan takes the ride on this genuine hold-up horse who has winning and placing form at 12f, though the redistribution note means he may find himself closer to the pace than ideal; good-ground record is mixed but form figures of 85-252 show consistent involvement.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last five starts yet twice a runner-up in that spell, Jimmy Mark shows consistency without a win to show for it; he has run over today's trip and going before, though 136 lb is a stiff enough burden for a horse rated just 56 officially.

runners_data.name: Praise Indeed
runners_data.note: Won over 10f on good ground and has placed at that trip — the booking of Lewis Edmunds is modest but the horse has solid recent form at this course-going combination; true hold-up type who will need plenty of gaps to open in the straight.
runners_data.comment: Placed last time out but winless in her last five starts overall, Praise Indeed has experience of today's going and returns on a quick 21-day turnaround; the second is a bright spot, though consistency remains the issue at a mark of 53.

runners_data.name: Grindleton
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides the race's sole confirmed front-runner for the Kubler yard, 63 days off the track is the one query; no good-going win to his name in six attempts but uncontested lead on a fair surface at 1m4f suits his role perfectly.
runners_data.comment: Ran a fine second two starts back and third four starts back, giving him a solid profile heading into this; our rating of 65 ranks him second in the field. The main risk is that eighth last time out after 63 days off.

runners_data.name: Ada Rose
runners_data.note: Kevin Philippart de Foy's filly won over 12f at Sandown in June, David Egan a high-class booking; 49 days since that win, and while she's shown hold-up tendencies she has the tactical speed and winning form at this trip to feature prominently.
runners_data.comment: Ada Rose won last time out but has been inconsistent in recent starts, with a ninth two starts back sitting awkwardly in her record. She has run over today's trip, though our figures rank her eighth of ten, making her hard to fancy at these weights.

runners_data.name: Pomeriggio
runners_data.note: Nikki Evans runner with a ⚠ fades-in-finish flag — Ryan Kavanagh claims 3lbs but the horse's record shows a tendency to fade, and being a natural hold-up type shoe-horned into midfield only increases the risk of a one-paced effort; recent form figures of 830-97 are uninspiring.
runners_data.comment: Winless in her last five starts, Pomeriggio's best recent effort was a third four starts back, though she returns after a 50-day absence and has run over today's distance and going before; at 126 lb off an official mark of 45, she is hard to fancy from mid-division.

runners_data.name: Houndswood Willow
runners_data.note: Tom Dascombe's 3yo has shown only modest form at 10-12f on soft/good ground and William Cox rides; the horse's natural hold-up style is compromised by the congested field, and trainer has sent out 0 winners from 8 runners in the last 14 days — proceed with caution.
runners_data.comment: Houndswood Willow has run over today's trip and going, returns on a fresh 27-day break, and our rating of 63 suggests he's better than his official mark of 55 — a lively threat. The risk is he's winless in his last five starts.

runners_data.name: A Daughters Love
runners_data.note: Jack Doughty rides a horse whose record shows two recent wins at 10f on good ground (form: 331150) — the class angle is clear; despite being a hold-up type in profile, the horse has raced handily in practice and could push forward to sit close behind Grindleton, making it the most dangerous redistributed runner in the field.
runners_data.comment: Back-to-back unplaced runs in her last two starts make A Daughters Love hard to fancy here, ranked ninth of ten on our figures; she has experience of today's trip and conditions, and her two wins in her last six starts show ability, but the current form is a concern.

runners_data.name: Cartrefle
runners_data.note: Ed de Giles's 3yo has only three runs on record, all in soft or slow conditions, and carries the ⚠ fades-in-finish flag; Molly Gunn (5lb claim) is a positive on weight but the horse's limited CV, preference for headgear (hg:p), and lack of good-ground evidence make this a significant ask.
runners_data.comment: Winless in his last three starts, with back-to-back unplaced efforts his most recent form, Cartrefle arrives 56 days off the track and ranked bottom of the field on our figures — hard to make a case for him here.

races.paceDynamic: Grindleton is the sole confirmed front-runner and, with Tom Marquand aboard, will stride out from the front at a controlled, sustainable gallop over this 1m4f trip on good ground — there is no genuine rival to press or disrupt him, so the pace is likely to be measured rather than searching. Behind him, a congested mass of hold-up horses — Jimmy Mark, Houndswood Willow, A Daughters Love, Praise Indeed, Pomeriggio, and Cartrefle — are all natural closers who have been redistributed into midfield slots because the map cannot accommodate them all at the rear; of those, A Daughters Love (winning form at 10f on good, races handily in practice) and Jimmy Mark are the most likely to actually secure a prominent berth ahead of the true hold-up brigade. The field contains more pace-shy types than a single front-runner can stretch, meaning Grindleton dictates from the front, the midfield clusters tightly, and the race will be decided by who can pick up quickest off a modest tempo in the straight. This shape strongly favours horses who can sit just off the pace, travel smoothly, and produce a sustained late challenge — pure hold-up horses relying on a fast-run race to get them into it will be disappointed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Grindleton Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Grindleton is allowed to bowl along at a sedate pace and the field behind him clumps together without a serious challenge forming early.
scenarios.body: Grindleton dictates every yard at a comfortable clip, the field strings out passively, and runners who can travel smoothly just off the pace and pick up in the straight benefit most; horses forced wide or trapped in a midfield squeeze are disadvantaged.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Steal It
scenarios.trigger: If A Daughters Love or Jimmy Mark aggressively push forward to sit close to Grindleton and the real closers cannot peel out in time.
scenarios.body: A contested pace develops between two or three near the front, honest gallop is set from the start, and the stamina-laden front two fight it out in the home straight; hold-up horses never get close enough.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closers Deliver Late
scenarios.trigger: If Grindleton's pace is slow enough to compress the field but a late rush of energy in the straight allows true hold-up horses to sweep through.
scenarios.body: A bunched midfield creates a sprint-finish scenario over the final 2f and horses with the highest finishing speed get the gaps late; this is a lower-probability shape because most of the genuine closers are redistributed and cannot guarantee getting back far enough.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Moderate Pace Collapses
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart tactically — a false crawl causes traffic problems and bunching, and the first two home come from completely unexpected positions.
scenarios.body: Grindleton's sedate front-running tempo creates a chaotic sprint home with multiple horses in contention, rewarding those drawn or positioned with the clearest run at the 2f pole; form is largely irrelevant in this shape.

watchPoints.text: Watch Grindleton's early position — if Tom Marquand is pushed wide or denied a clean break from the gate, the entire race shape collapses and the compressed midfield becomes a free-for-all.

A Daughters Love (Jack Doughty) could push forward aggressively given her winning form at 10f on good; if she challenges Grindleton for the front, the pace increases materially and true hold-up horses benefit late.

Condotti with Oisin Murphy is the standout jockey booking and the combination of 1m4f step-up plus good ground suits — watch for Murphy angling for a clean run from off the pace at the 3f pole where traffic is likely to form.

With six of ten runners being genuine hold-up types redistributed into midfield, the 2f-out point will be heavily congested — any horse drawn towards the outside (clear passage) gains a significant positional advantage over those trapped on the rail.

Pomeriggio and Cartrefle both carry the fades-in-finish flag and are at the bottom of the weights — in a race with a slow early pace and a sprint finish, both face the worst possible scenario and should be considered vulnerable in any in-running assessment.
